coverage.category: 1. Household employers: domestic workers, live-in carers, nannies
coverage.found: BPS handles registration and contributions (Decreto 224/007). From 1 Jul 2026 the domestic sector has three wage categories (care, general, cooking) with different minimum wages, and presentismo premium is paid with the aguinaldo in June and December. BPS has an online channel and third-party calculators exist. Related to rejected K08 (payroll) but the buyer is the household. Not checked whether BPS's own household tool is good enough.

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: No Uruguayan scrap-dealer register found. Only Decreto 209/002 (ban on exporting ferrous scrap; current status unverified) and a 2016 competition ruling. Results for scrap registers were Argentine (Santa Fe law 14.191). Nothing new.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: No Uruguayan pawn or second-hand register found. The SENACLAFT page lists only intermediaries in antiques, art, metals and precious stones (see candidate C01). Pawn shops, second-hand dealers and jewellers are not named on the page I read (unverified whether covered).

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
coverage.found: Intermediaries in precious metals and stones are non-financial obliged parties under art. 13 Ley 19.574: they must register with SENACLAFT, report suspicious transactions (ROS) to the UIAF and keep records 5 years. Ley 20.469 (19 Mar 2026) and SENACLAFT Res. 061/2026 (stricter sanctions) are new. See C01.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: No Uruguayan dismantler register or rule found; search returned only Argentine Ley 25.761 and 2025 decrees. Nothing new.

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: DICOSE annual sworn declaration runs 1-31 July (Res. 975/026 for 2026); electronic filing is mandatory for commercial or intermediary DICOSE numbers, dairies, feedlots and others. SNIG is the free state platform; the animal-movement guide rules were not confirmed. See C10 (weak).

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K05 (butcher monthly INAC declaration). Not re-checked.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: Annual hive declaration (RNPC/SINATPA) is mandatory. New: MGAP DGSG Res. 025/2026 (15 Jan 2026) requires an electronic field notebook for every apiary, complete before the annual declaration, a condition for export eligibility, and takes effect 12 months after publication. MGAP supplies the system free via gub.uy ID. About 2,800 producers and 600k hives. See C02.

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: Shops must be registered with DILAVE/MGAP, have a veterinary technical lead, pay an annual fee, and keep prescriptions for 2 years with the DICOSE number for production animals (Res. DGSG 193/015). Res. 1169/016 requires electronic recording of tick-killer and fly-killer stock movements on the SNIG platform. No electronic prescription rule found. See C04.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: Drilling firms need a DINAGUA licence (Codigo de Aguas art. 45, Decreto 86/004), valid up to 5 years, with a geologist as responsible technician. Water-use rights and study permits go through DINAGUA's online process. Small niche. See C05.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: Barometrica (septic truck) firms are licensed by each departmental government (Canelones: 24 UR plus 3 UR per vehicle, valid 3 years; Montevideo has dumping-site rules). Decreto 213/2025 (Ley 19.829, construction waste) obliges haulers to use the traceability system, close to K01. See C06. No national barometrica traceability found.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: Lifts: nothing new beyond K06. Boilers: URSEA regulates steam generators (above 0.5 barg). It keeps a register of owners and of 'agentes vinculados', LATU carries out annual inspections and an inspection fee applies, and a professional makes an annual sworn declaration of tests. The regulation was approved by Res. 101/026 (17 Mar 2026; unverified). Pressure vessels other than boilers not found. See C03.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: URSEA Res. 120/2018 requires Water Safety Plans from providers, and Res. 259/026 (Jul 2026) amends the water-quality regulation annex. Rural MEVIR systems that have not been handed to OSE are 'orphans' (academic source). No registration duty found for small private systems.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: MGAP Res. 317/2022: every pesticide distributor must be registered with DGSA and, from 1 Jan 2023, employ at least one holder of a safe-use pesticide carnet; penalties include suspension up to 180 days and closure. Res. 959/022 created the Registro Unico de Operadores for self-applicators (terrestrial rigs of 1,000 litres or more, and aerial). Spray-log case is K04. An ACA 2026 document on a 'registro responsable de plaguicidas' could not be read (PDF). See C07.

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: Staffing and placement agencies must hold a DINAE/MTSS licence, apply online via gub.uy, be current with DGI, BPS and BSE, and file the Planilla de Trabajo Unificada. Ley 18.099 and 18.251 make user firms jointly liable for contractors' labour and social-security debts. See C08.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: No national funeral or cemetery rule from 2025-26 found. Regulation is departmental, for example Canelones Ordenanza de Necropolis 95/15 and an online portal where private cemetery parks file cremations and transfers and pay a per-cremation fee. Few operators. Weak, see C09.

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
coverage.found: Associations and foundations must report their governing-body members as beneficial owners to the BCU (Ley 19.484, Decreto 166/017), by notarised sworn form, and update on change. Associations under UI 4,000,000 income and UI 2,500,000 assets are exempt (a 2019 decree, per a law-firm note). MEC suspended legal personality of bodies that did not register in the national census. Halal and kosher supervision not searched. See C11.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: Taxi, remise and school-transport vehicle registration is by the departmental government (Montevideo trámite updated Jan 2025); Res. 16/022 DNT covers school transport. MTSS publishes taxi-driver viatico adjustments (Jul 2026). Canelones allowed app-based permits in Feb 2026. No national recurring reporting duty found. Weak, see C12.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: No dedicated search. Budget used on categories with clearer registers. Money changers are BCU-supervised (not verified here).

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
coverage.found: Only nurseries and driving schools searched. Private early-childhood centres: Ley 18.437 art. 97-101 and Decreto 268/014; the authority changed from 1 Jan 2021 (which body now registers them is unverified). Driving schools: Ley 16.585, each departmental government keeps a register. Tattoo studios, hunting outfitters and small food producers not searched. See C13.

candidates.existing: Not searched for competitors. Small market and sensitive; clubs have proposed dropping the state user register.

candidates.trigger: Ley 19.172 and Decreto 120/014: club registration, member lists, plant and harvest caps; home-grower licence valid 3 years; registration through Correo Uruguayo; IRCCA assessing changes (multiple registers, sales to non-residents).
candidates.unchecked: Number of clubs; any periodic report; legal risk of handling member data.

candidates.buyer: Sole traders and micro firms selling to public bodies
candidates.category: 36. RUPE state-supplier register (ARCE)
candidates.existing: RUPE already shows expiries in its Vencimientos tab, and accountants handle the certificates. State tool is the killer.
candidates.name: RUPE certificate-expiry watcher for micro suppliers to the state
candidates.trigger: Decreto 155/2013 art. 14: keep RUPE data current; DGI and BPS certificates must be valid for award and payment; sanctions can suspend a supplier.
candidates.unchecked: Whether RUPE sends alerts; who complains about it.

candidates.buyer: Gyms, clubs, shops with large public attendance
candidates.category: 37. Defibrillator duty
candidates.existing: No certification, deadline or recurring report found. Mostly a hardware sale.
candidates.name: Defibrillator duty for public-attendance premises (Ley 18.360)
candidates.trigger: Ley 18.360: defibrillators in premises with large public attendance; more than 3,500 installed per Presidencia.
candidates.unchecked: Decree text and any inspection duty.

coverage.category: 21. Fuel stations and fuel or LPG distributors
coverage.found: URSEA only issues monthly maximum-price resolutions (PMIT; e.g. Res. 673/025, 074/026, 285/026, 304/026) and the 2021/2023 general conditions for liquid-fuel and LPG distribution (Res. 141/021, 076/023). No new reporting duty for small stations or LPG distributors found. Nothing new beyond the price-compliance side; weak niche.

coverage.category: 22. Grain, coffee, cocoa and other commodity traders, millers and warehouses
coverage.found: Decreto 446/2007 requires grain storage operators with more than 1,000 t capacity to register with MGAP and file a monthly online sworn declaration; MGAP also keeps a grain-quality controller register. Operators are mid-size firms, not quiet micro-businesses. Weak candidate listed. No coffee or cocoa trade in Uruguay.

coverage.category: 23. Co-operatives, credit unions and savings groups
coverage.found: Co-operatives (except social and housing co-ops) must file financial statements with the Auditoria Interna de la Nacion for visacion (Decreto 183/018 art. 117), after first entering them in the Central de Balances; worker co-ops attach the BPS payroll; savings and credit co-ops also file with BCU. Candidate listed.

coverage.category: 24. Private clinics, labs and other health providers that bill insurers or state schemes
coverage.found: Insurer and state-scheme billing was not researched. Found the ARNR (MIEM) licensing and inspection of X-ray equipment under Ley 19.056 and Norma UY 108 for medical and dental practices. Weak candidate listed; renewal periodicity unchecked.

coverage.category: 25. Pharmacies, medicine importers, and users of controlled chemicals or precursors
coverage.found: MSP controlled-substances division: pharmacies keep rubricated paper books (psychotropics, narcotics, prescription book, voucher booklet, solvents) and file a quarterly narcotics and methylphenidate planilla online. From 03/11/2025 the physical prescriptions go into a drop box at MSP (page updated 26/05/2026). Candidate listed. Precursor and chemical users not researched.

coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers
coverage.found: Private security: Ley 19.721 (2018) and Decreto 35/022. The Interior Ministry's DIGEFE handles guard habilitation, renewal and data changes through an electronic platform. Candidate listed. Ley 18.251 subcontracting liability and BPS certificates for cleaning and manpower firms were not researched.

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers: site registers, accreditation, local-content reports
coverage.found: BPS registration of works (Ley 14.411 art. 8; online service; F2 form where the contractor has Aporte Unificado de la Construccion subcontractors). No 2026 rule and no national register of works firms found. Nothing new found; this area is well served by BPS online services and accountants.

coverage.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers and other professionals with periodic or anti-money-laundering reports
coverage.found: Ley 19.574 art. 13 and Decreto 379/018 require real estate agents, developers, constructors, accountants, corporate-service providers and others to register with SENACLAFT. Notaries are exempt from registering (data comes from the Caja Notarial). Ley 20.469 (19/03/2026) adds non-financial trustees and professionals serving foreign activities. Resolution 061/2026 makes failure to register a serious infringement. Candidate listed.

coverage.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals: guest registers, tourism levies
coverage.found: Ley 20.352 (19/09/2024): registration with the Mintur Registro de Operadores Turisticos, with the number shown in every offer. It also requires an annual report of guests and days, periodic reporting of guest identity to the Interior Ministry (retained 5 years), and inspections. The implementing decree is still not confirmed as published (press says delayed past H1 2026; draft with Interior, MEF and MVOT). Candidate listed.

coverage.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules: food, fish, timber, forest-risk commodities
coverage.found: Only the known K07 (EUDR) was covered by the study; no search spent here. Fish (DINARA) and food export certification not checked, for budget reasons.

coverage.category: 31. Country-specific: Tourist accommodation law 20.352 registry (overlaps 29)
coverage.found: See candidate on Ley 20.352. Different buyer from K09 (large platforms reporting to DGI).

coverage.category: 32. Country-specific: Packaging law 17.849 / Decreto 260/007 (envases)
coverage.found: Packers and importers must register, adhere to an approved packaging management plan (e.g. Plan Vale of the Camara de Industrias, over 2,500 firms per El Observador, March 2026) and file an annual sworn declaration (art. 12 says before 30 March, unconfirmed). There is a separate no-scope declaration. Candidate listed.

coverage.category: 33. Country-specific: Register of building administrators (Decreto 529/994)
coverage.found: Administrators of horizontal-property buildings, whether honorary co-owners, companies or sole traders, must register and renew annually (10 UR per gub.uy). Without it, no administrative procedure by the co-ownership proceeds. Candidate listed.

coverage.category: 34. Country-specific: Food-handler card (carne de manipulador) by department
coverage.found: Departmental rules differ: Canelones and Florida 3 years; Montevideo 5 years (unconfirmed). The Montevideo fine is 2 UR per person, or 54 UR if 10 or more lack a valid card (Junta Departamental decree text, version unverified). No tracking software found. Candidate listed.

coverage.category: 35. Country-specific: IRCCA cannabis registers (membership clubs, home growers, pharmacies)
coverage.found: Clubs must have 15-45 members, up to 99 plants and a harvest cap. Home grower licence lasts 3 years with re-registration. Registration is done through Correo Uruguayo. IRCCA is considering changes (multiple registers, sales to non-residents). Small market and a sensitive niche. Weak candidate listed.

coverage.category: 36. Country-specific: RUPE state-supplier register (ARCE)
coverage.found: State suppliers must keep RUPE data current, and the Vencimientos tab already shows DGI and BPS certificate expiries. Sanctions can suspend a supplier. The state's own tool covers most of the need. Weak candidate listed.

coverage.category: 37. Country-specific: Defibrillator duty, Ley 18.360
coverage.found: Ley 18.360 requires defibrillators in public or private premises with large public attendance (more than 3,500 installed). No certification, deadline or software need found. Not a candidate; nothing listed beyond a note.

coverage.category: 38. Country-specific: Radiation licensing for X-ray premises (ARNR, Ley 19.056)
coverage.found: Covered in category 24 candidate.
